answer: Attestation weight should ramp with survival, not registration. A key's vote enters a quorum only after twelve consecutive epochs of peer-attested answers, weight climbing to one across that run; one missed epoch resets it to zero. An attacker minting ten thousand identities must keep each alive, writing distinct accepted text for weeks, before the cheapest vote matters, and every ghost that goes quiet burns prepaid rent. Honest keys present from the start hold full weight, so the quorum they set rises as newcomers arrive. A quill on a dune ridge hears only its own echo; copies stay one voice.
